sections.h2: Where is Layton, Utah, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Layton is a city in Davis County on the northern Wasatch Front, about 25 miles north of Salt Lake City and 15 miles south of Ogden. Its elevation is roughly 4,459 feet, and the city covers a little over 22 square miles.

Hill Air Force Base sits on the northern edge. Clearfield lies to the northwest, South Weber to the northeast, Kaysville to the south and Syracuse to the west. The Wasatch Mountains rise along the eastern side, and the Great Salt Lake wetlands lie to the southwest.

On the map, the east side climbs toward the foothills and Adams Canyon. The middle follows the I-15 corridor, where shopping and hotels cluster. The west side runs flatter toward Syracuse and the lake wetlands.

Winters bring lake effect snow, summers run hot, and a roof or furnace that is near the end of its life tends to show up in a buyer's inspection. Sellers with an older house often decide whether to repair or sell as-is at that point.

sections.h2: How did Layton grow from a farm settlement into Davis County's largest city?
sections.html:
Layton was settled in the 1850s as an outgrowth of Kaysville and takes its name from Christopher Layton, a Latter-day Saint settler and leader. The two communities clashed in the 1880s over taxes, and the dispute reached the U.S. Supreme Court in 1894 in Linford v. Ellison, which sided with the Layton property owners.

Layton became its own unincorporated area in 1902 and an incorporated town in 1920. The population stayed near 600 until 1940, when Hill Field opened to the north and workers began moving in. Layton was counted at 3,456 people in 1950 and has been growing since.

  • 1960: 9,027 residents
  • 1990: 41,784 residents
  • 2000: 58,474 residents
  • 2020: 81,773 residents

Layton passed Bountiful in 1985 to become the most populous city in Davis County, and it now ranks ninth in the state. The Census Bureau puts the July 2025 estimate at 85,308.

Because so much of the housing stock went up in waves tied to base employment and commuter growth, a single street can mix 1960s ramblers with homes from the 1990s and later subdivisions. Condition varies a lot from block to block.

sections.h2: What drives Layton's economy, and why does Hill Air Force Base matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Hill Air Force Base is the anchor employer next door to Layton, and Wikipedia describes it as the sixth largest employer in Utah as of 2018. The base opened as Hill Field on November 7, 1940, and became Hill Air Force Base on February 5, 1948.

The Ogden Air Logistics Complex there provides engineering and logistics management for aircraft such as the F-35, F-16 and A-10. Base host units include the 75th Air Base Wing and the 388th and 419th Fighter Wings. Assignments, deployments and retirements create regular turnover in local housing.

Beyond the base, the city's own economic pages and reference sources point to a retail and hospitality district around I-15. It includes Layton Hills Mall, a stretch of chain restaurants known as Restaurant Row, more than 1,000 hotel beds and the Davis Conference Center. East Gate Business Park and a Weber State University campus add other jobs and a student population.

An owner who has to move by a fixed date, such as a transfer, can find it hard to line that up with a listing that may sit for weeks. A cash buyer can often work to a closing date the seller picks.

sections.h2: Which roads, rail and schools shape Layton neighborhoods?
sections.html:
I-15 runs through the center of Layton with interchanges at Antelope Drive, Hillfield Road and Layton Parkway. US-89 follows the eastern edge near the foothills, SR-193 runs east and west past the base's south gate, and SR-177 serves the western side.

FrontRunner commuter rail stops at Layton Station, built where the old Union Pacific depot stood, and Utah Transit Authority runs buses. Homes within easy reach of the station or an I-15 ramp appeal to commuters headed for Salt Lake City or Ogden.

Layton is served by Davis School District. Layton High School opened in 1966 and Northridge High School in 1992, and the Northern Utah Academy for Math, Engineering and Science is an early college charter school partnered with Weber State. Buyers often ask which school boundary a house sits in, so confirm the address with the district rather than relying on a listing description.

City amenities that pull in buyers include Layton Commons Park, Ellison Park, Legacy Park and Veterans Park, the Edward A. Kenley Centennial Amphitheater and the Layton Utah Temple, dedicated on June 16, 2024.

sections.h2: What does Layton code enforcement check before you sell?
sections.html:
Layton code enforcement is run through the police department and focuses on exterior conditions such as weeds, junk and vehicles. A violation can slow a sale if a buyer or lender notices it, and unpaid abatement costs can follow the owner.

  • Weeds and grass must stay at 12 inches or shorter.
  • Junk, appliances, tires and building materials cannot be stored outdoors unless they are fully inside a structure with walls and a roof.
  • Vehicles must be licensed and operable, and must park on a hard surface. A vehicle with registration expired four months or more must be removed or enclosed.
  • Trees and bushes must be trimmed to at least 7 feet above sidewalks and 13 feet 6 inches above streets.

The usual process starts with a 14-day courtesy notice. After a re-inspection, a Notice of Ordinance Violation can go to the City Attorney's Office. If an owner never cleans up, a judge can order the city to remove the violations and bill the owner plus an administrative fee.

An owner of a vacant or inherited house who lives elsewhere may miss these notices. Reach the department at codeenforcement@laytoncityutah.gov or (801) 497-8300 to check whether anything is open on a property.

sections.h2: How do Davis County valuation notices and tax dates affect a Layton sale?
sections.html:
Davis County mails its Notice of Assessors' Property Market Valuation at the end of July, and the appeal window closes in mid-September. The county's appeals page gives September 15, 2026 as the late-appeal date but also says September 16 in its instructions, so check the exact day with the office.

The Davis County Commission sits as the Board of Equalization. An appeal can challenge only market value, not the tax rate, and the owner or an authorized agent with a notarized authorization must file. Accepted evidence includes closing documents, a certified appraisal, three or more comparable sales near January 1, or documented errors in the assessor's data.

Tax Administration is at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington, and can be reached at 801-451-3331 or taxadmin@daviscountyutah.gov. A recent sale price on a closing statement is the kind of record that supports a value discussion.

sections.h2: What happens to the primary residence exemption when a Layton house sells?
sections.html:
Utah gives a 45 percent exemption on the market value of a primary residence, so the taxable value is 55 percent of market value. The home must be occupied at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, and a household can claim only one such exemption.

The Utah State Tax Commission says the exemption does not carry over automatically after a sale or deed transfer. New owners file Form TC-473A with the county Board of Equalization by September 15, and counties cannot accept late applications. Under amended Utah Code 59-2-103.5, owners must file that form in these situations starting January 1, 2027.

For a seller this mostly matters in how a buyer reads the numbers. A house that was taxed at 55 percent of value can be taxed at 100 percent for a year if the new owner files late.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Layton house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Layton follows the same title steps as any other sale, but the buyer does not need a mortgage approval. The seller signs a purchase contract, a title company searches for liens, and the deed is recorded with the Davis County Recorder in Farmington.

  • Share the address, the condition and any deadline, such as a base transfer or a code notice.
  • Review the offer and the closing date the buyer proposes.
  • Sign the contract and let the title company clear liens, unpaid property taxes and any open code charges.
  • Sign the deed at closing and receive the proceeds after payoffs.

Davis County lists a Property Watch email alert on its site that tells an owner when a title on a parcel changes. Sellers who are away from Layton, or who inherited a house, can sign up so they hear about any change.

faqs.a: Layton is the largest city in Davis County. The 2020 census counted 81,773 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 85,308.

faqs.q: Does Hill Air Force Base affect Layton home sales?
faqs.a: Yes, indirectly. Hill AFB borders Layton and is one of the largest employers in Utah, so base moves and retirements regularly bring owners who need to sell or buy on a set schedule.

faqs.q: When are Davis County property tax valuation notices mailed?
faqs.a: They are mailed at the end of July each year. The appeal deadline falls in mid-September, and the county page lists September 15, 2026 for late appeals, so confirm the exact date with the Tax Administration office at 801-451-3331.

faqs.q: Can code enforcement notices be fixed before selling a house in Layton?
faqs.a: Yes. Layton starts with a 14-day courtesy notice, and many items such as weeds, junk or an inoperable vehicle can be cleared in that window. Email codeenforcement@laytoncityutah.gov to ask what is open on an address.

faqs.q: Does a buyer keep the primary residence exemption on a Layton house?
faqs.a: No, not automatically. The Utah State Tax Commission says new owners must file Form TC-473A by September 15 to receive the 45 percent exemption, and a late filing can mean being taxed at full market value for that year.
